event: He wakes before dawn; the coals pulse, and the old man sits on his log, his hands still.
The mountain's cold is still in his bones, and the morning carries its own chill.
Guardian Sword across his back, Slate at his hip, the broken hilt in his pack by the pot.
"The Temple," the old man says without turning. "Follow the path east. You'll see it."
The spire has been his bearing point since the first morning, rising above the treeline.
Grass silver with dew, the green smell of morning: he can feel this is the last one.
The Temple of Time: rows of cracked dark columns, no roof, shafts of light sliding on stone.
His stride slows to reverence; the echoes come back softened, as if the floor could hear.
The Goddess Statue fills the apse: three times his height, eyes closed, cupped hands empty.
Moss on her fingers, grass at her base; nobody has knelt here in a century.
The Slate gives a low, resonant chime, and the four Spirit Orbs stir warm inside it.
They lean toward the Statue as he nears, pulsing in unison on the screen.
Her cupped hands begin to glow a warm gold.
A vast, warm presence speaks: I can see the light of the Goddess in your eyes.
Something sees him: not as hero, not as the boy from the shrine, but as worth addressing.
Which do you desire? Two streams of light: a red heart, and a green spiral, turning.
Three hearts have left him staggering at every blow; his hand moves to the heart.
It is no bold choice, but a humbled one. He chooses to endure.
The four orbs lift from the Slate in a slow spiral into her hands, and the gold flares.

changes.note: Four Spirit Orbs offered to the Goddess Statue

event: One point of warmth settles into his chest, a deepening, and his breath goes further.
The Slate: Heart Container received. Hearts 3 to 4. Stamina: 1 wheel.

changes.note: The new heart comes full: four hearts

event: The glow fades to stone, and the presence settles back into its patience: Go in peace.
He lingers as the shafts of sun slide across the floor.
At the eastern wall he climbs the broken inner stairs, with his hands where feet won't do.
The stairs open on a gallery whose outer edge has broken away onto all of Hyrule.
Gold and green fields, bright rivers, roads like pale threads, and the Castle's dark shroud.
The old man sits on the gallery's edge, hood down for the first time, his white hair thin.
"You made the trade," he says, without turning.
Link sits beside him on sun-warmed stone; from here the Statue looks smaller.
The old man's hands tremble in his lap: "I have something to tell you."
"This kingdom was called Hyrule. It still is, though precious little is left of the name."
"A hundred years ago it was whole: a castle, a court, and in the court, a king."
Link sees the old man's shadow on the stone is wrong: taller, broader at the crown.
He looks from the shadow to the old man and back, and the old man sees him looking.
"You see it," the old man says quietly, almost with relief, and exhales.
The rough cloak thins to robes of state in deep blue and gold; the hood becomes a crown.
His hands are no longer flesh; a pale gold ghost-light shines through them.
"I am King Rhoam Bosphoramus Hyrule."
Link does not move; his hand has gone to the Slate, the one thing joining then to now.
"This kingdom had a champion, a knight chosen by the Goddess's own sword."
"A hundred years ago the Calamity returned: Ganon, a being of ancient malice."
"It corrupted our guardians." The machines on the Plateau were the fallen kingdom's own.
"The Divine Beasts, four great constructs, each piloted by a champion. Ganon took them all."
"The champions fell. The hero fell." The flatness in his voice is the only other road to weeping.
"The princess carried him to the Shrine where you woke, and then she sealed Ganon."
Link's body turns toward the Castle on its own, an instinct below memory.
"She has held him alone for a hundred years. I could not help her. But you can."
"You are that hero, brought to the Shrine near death a hundred years ago, sleeping, healing."
"Your memories will return. In time. In pieces. The Slate may help."
"Free the Divine Beasts. Find the champions' spirits. Turn their power on the Calamity."
"Then go to the Castle. Save my daughter." The last three words are the father's.
Silence. Link sits with the weight of it, reorganising everything he thought he knew.
Four shrines, four monks, four orbs for one heart, and four nights by the fire with a king.
He breathes, and the breath goes further than it used to. Four hearts now.
"I have one last thing for you." From his robes the king draws the folded paraglider.
"Not payment. A provision, from someone who cannot walk the road with you."
Link takes it: worn smooth at the grips, dark with age, weighing almost nothing.

changes.note: King Rhoam gives Link the paraglider

event: The Slate: Paraglider acquired. Hold to deploy in freefall; stamina is spent in flight.
"Be careful. And eat something before you go. You're too thin."
The ghost-light flickers, and the corner of his mouth almost makes a smile.
He turns toward the Castle, as a man looks at a house he lived in once.
Then King Rhoam begins to fade, gently, the way a fire burns down when nobody feeds it.
His robes and crown dim, the morning shows through him, and what may be trust goes last.
The light that was King Rhoam rises and joins the morning; the gallery is empty.
Link sits alone with the paraglider and the Slate, the kingdom below, the mission in his chest.
He climbs down past the Goddess Statue and out through the broken entrance into morning.
The Plateau is quiet; the wind moves through the grass in its oldest habit.
He walks to the edge, where the cliffs fall away hundreds of meters, sheer.
The paraglider's frame unfolds in his hands, its joints clicking into place.
He pauses, not from fear but from awareness: he is four days old.
Below lies a fallen kingdom, and a castle where a princess has held a demon for a century.
Warm wind rises from below; the twin peaks frame a pass south, toward someone named Impa.
He raises the paraglider over his head, and the canvas catches the wind and pulls.
He steps off the edge.
The Plateau shrinks behind and above him as the canvas catches the rising air and holds.
The stamina gauge at the Slate's edge flickers, draining steadily; his shoulders burn.
Below him all of Hyrule: wild golden grass, rivers, forests, ruins, and roads going south.
The air tastes alive, and beneath it, faint, a low pulse from the Castle: the Malice's heartbeat.
His stamina drains, his grip tightens, and the ground comes up green and soft.
His feet touch waist-high wild grass in the fields below; he stands in it and breathes.
Behind him the Plateau is a mesa against the morning sky; the road runs south to the twin peaks.
The Slate pulses once: the map updates, the known world one step wider.
The tutorial is over. The world has begun. He walks into the grass, the sun warm on his face.
